correctness.rationale: Definitions, quantifiers, range 0<=s<=log n and exact normalizations are fixed. The proof reproduces the connectivity-window isolate lemma by factorial moments and a spanning-tree union bound; a two-replica marked-isolation factorial-moment argument establishes the crucial joint law, which in turn supplies conditional L² profile convergence. An explicit isolate-variance bound controls the entire integrated tail in L². A standard-library checker passed 226 exact/numerical assertions on independent finite expressions; such computations do not certify the infinite argument.

value.rationale: The source poses the natural Erdős–Rényi average-reliability question. In its connectivity window, the non-self-averaging phenomenon is not an arbitrary sliced statistic: reliability is exactly zero for disconnected networks, and the theorem identifies the sharp conditional area, full near-unit retention curve and a strictly positive limiting ensemble variance. This distinction is useful when interpreting robustness of random network realizations. The first moment alone is recognized as implied by classical connectivity and is not relied upon to justify value.
